_comment: Same transfer as text_rebase_t5base_t5large_theseus_hubcheckpoint.json, but method=steer_text instead of theseus. steer_text never writes B's backbone weights -- it fits a feature-space correction and adds it at eval time -- so B's backbone is identical (pretrained, untouched) for both the target_zeroshot baseline and the corrected condition.
_source_head: source_task_heads is NOT set on purpose: varun-v-rao/t5-base-snli already contains its own real fine-tuned classification_head.* weights, loaded automatically by TextLM.build when _load_tuned_source_state_dict detects the tuned_ckpts entry is a full Hub model -- steer_text.prepare() reads w_a straight off that live head.
_source_input_template: varun-v-rao/t5-base-snli was fine-tuned on a single formatted string, not this repo's default tokenizer(premise, hypothesis) pair encoding -- confirmed with scripts/probe_nli_input_format.py (pair encoding: ~0.35 accuracy / chance; this template: ~0.91, matching the model card's claimed 0.8982). This is A-only: B (t5-v1_1-large) still uses the default pair encoding.
_block_ridge_note: feature_regime=linear + stage_2_strategy=block_ridge groups B's 24 residual blocks down (block_group_strategy=concat) to match A's 12, so every one of B's blocks participates in the fit, not just a name-matching prefix. The forward-mode jvp this needs linearizes A (t5-base, ~220M params, 12 layers), NOT B -- affordable, well under steer_text's own 500M-parameter warning threshold. If this is too slow/memory-heavy on your allocation, fall back to feature_regime=standard + stage_2_strategy=global_ridge (see configs/text_rebase_t5_steer.json).
_cache_note: feature_cache_dir keys features by source_tag/target_tag/task/regime/split; source_tag comes from source_model_name_or_path (google-t5__t5-base here), so this never collides with a cache built from a different A (e.g. google/t5-v1_1-base in text_rebase_t5base_t5large_steer_nearestmean.json).
